failure_summary.description: Chose a nearby related person despite the same-clue parenthetical identifying the answer; the existing evidence-priority rule was not followed.
Returned a country where the fragment calls for the corresponding adjective or demonym.
Gave semantically correct answers with redundant generic category wording instead of the concise conventional answer form.

patch.reasoning: The skill already covers prioritizing explicit same-clue evidence, so no duplicate rule is needed for that failure. Clarifying that answers should match the clue's grammatical form and omit generic category words addresses the country-versus-demonym mismatch and the two unnecessarily expanded answers.

edits.target: - Give the shortest unambiguous answer at the requested granularity, using the concise form most directly supported by the clue and its evidence. Do not add an unnecessary corporate suffix or title subtitle, or repeat wording already supplied by the clue. For a person, use an explicitly supported full personal name rather than substituting a familiar nickname when the full name is the relevant answer. When a category is already specified, provide the distinguishing value rather than repeating the category.
edits.content: - Give the shortest unambiguous answer at the requested granularity, in the conventional lexical form and part of speech called for by the clue (for example, an adjective or demonym rather than its associated country). When a clue already supplies the category or type, return the distinguishing value alone: do not append a generic category noun, institution label, title, explanatory wording, or suffix unless needed for disambiguation. For a person, use an explicitly supported full personal name rather than substituting a familiar nickname when the full name is relevant.
